title: Waiting for mangoes
text:
Laras had a mango tree in her garden. Every day after school, she ran outside to look at it. The mangoes were small and green.

'Are they ready yet?' she asked Grandpa.

'Not yet,' said Grandpa. 'Good things take time.'

Laras waited and waited. She counted the mangoes. There were twelve. She drew a picture of the tree in her notebook.

At last, one morning, the mangoes were big and yellow. Grandpa picked them with a long stick. Laras washed them, and Grandpa cut them into pieces. The mangoes were sweet and juicy.

Laras took six mangoes to her neighbours. 'That was a long wait,' she said, 'and these are the best mangoes ever!'
